# Michel Aljed (ميشيل الجد)

> Michel Aljed is an offensive security engineer and penetration tester based in Damascus, Syria. He tests web applications for security flaws, builds security tooling in Python and C++, and does empirical research in algorithms and machine learning.

Also known as: ميشيل الجد, ميشال الجد, Michel Al-Jed. Online handles: sand8storm (GitHub), sand666wind (HackerOne, Intigriti, Bugcrowd), cyborg.div (Instagram, Arabic-language security content).

## Focus
- Web application penetration testing (black-box, authorized engagements with Syrian organizations)
- OSINT-driven security assessments
- Bug bounty and responsible disclosure on HackerOne, Intigriti, and Bugcrowd
- Security tool development in Python and C++

## Tools
- [Beast403](https://github.com/sand8storm/Beast403): released 403/401 bypass scanner, accuracy first. Validates every candidate bypass against a live per-target oracle using SimHash structural classification, with a raw-socket engine to defeat client-side path normalization. 0 false positives across 28 negative targets.
- SSTIeye (in progress): server-side template injection scanner using randomized arithmetic probes confirmed against a baseline response.

## Research
- TSP heuristics, a systematic empirical study of 20+ construction, local-search, and metaheuristic methods with paired t-tests.
- LKH candidate generation, independent verification (MST ∪ Delaunay ∪ k-NN vs α-nearness).
- Riemann zeta zeros, autoencoder-based analysis of Odlyzko's dataset.

## Background
- B.Sc. Computer Engineering, Antioch Private Syrian University, Damascus (expected 2027)
- Reached the top 10 on TryHackMe in Syria
- Languages: Arabic (native), English (C1)
